headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line, yet shorts are the ones getting liquidated
paragraphs: Start with the map: all seven majors here trade below their 200-day averages, and none carries a golden cross. BTC is 47.9% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is 60.2% off its high, and the rest are further out still: SOL -69.2%, XRP -68.4%, BNB -53.8%, DOGE -75.8%, ADA -79.6%. That's a uniform picture, a market still digesting a long drawdown rather than opening a new leg up.

Layer momentum on top and a divergence shows up. RSI readings sit in the 50s and 60s for BTC (54.8), ETH (57.0), SOL (55.5), BNB (64.4) and ADA (64.8), and MACD sits above its signal line for five of the seven names (BTC, SOL, BNB, DOGE, ADA). Price below the long-term trend while short-term momentum turns constructive is a specific finding: it reads as a bounce inside a downtrend, not evidence the downtrend itself has ended. XRP (RSI 39.6, MACD still below signal) and DOGE (RSI 44.3) aren't participating in that bounce the same way.

Positioning explains part of the bounce. Funding, the periodic payment longs make to shorts (or vice versa) to hold a perpetual futures position, is cheap on the majors: 0.9% annualized on BTC, 3.3% on ETH. But SOL, XRP and DOGE all carry funding at 11% annualized, and their long/short account ratios confirm a crowded trade: 4.65 longs per short on DOGE, 3.68 on XRP, 2.15 on SOL. The last day of liquidations shows who paid for that crowding: SOL shorts lost $2.14M versus $148k for longs, ETH shorts lost $1.7M versus $406k for longs. A one-sided boat got rocked, and it moved price up rather than down.

Flows tell a mixed story depending on which coin you're watching. BTC spot ETFs took in $101.7M on 07 Aug 2026, the fifth straight session in that direction, for a five-session total of $865.3M, a traditional-finance bid that's held its direction for a full week. ETH ETFs added $49.6M the same day, but only four of the last five sessions agree, five-session net $243.7M, so calling that one a persistent trend would be getting ahead of the tape. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, sits at $306.2B, down 1.03% over the past month. On the exchange side, $302.6M in net value moved onto exchanges over the last 48 hours, but that headline is almost entirely ether: $309.7M of ETH flowed onto exchanges with zero offsetting outflow, including a single $165.7M leg to Coinbase. BTC actually moved the other way, $7.1M net off exchanges, with $118M leaving Kraken and $65.6M leaving Coinbase even as $115M went onto Coinbase Institutional and $102M onto Binance. The weekly whale series (-$146.9M, +$445.9M, +$1,075.3M, +$132.2M) has been net-positive three of the last four reads but is shrinking, a cooling trend rather than a reversal.

Set against all that, the Fear & Greed index reads 31, labeled Fear, sitting near the top of its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. A nervous crowd, ETFs still taking in bitcoin, and shorts getting run over in derivatives don't agree with each other, and that disagreement is the more interesting read than any single gauge. Worth watching from here: whether BTC's ETF streak holds a full week for ether too, whether SOL/XRP/DOGE funding cools off its 11% perch, whether the whale weekly series turns negative, or whether BTC actually reclaims its 200-day line rather than just testing momentum beneath it.
